error.cannot_connect: The AUX-2 port could not be opened. Check that the device is turned on and adopted in Home Assistant.
error.no_proxy_ports: No AUX-2 serial ports were found. Connect the Home Assistant Connect AUX-2 and adopt it in Home Assistant first.
error.port_busy: The AUX-2 port is already in use. Close whatever else holds it open and try again.
error.serial_support_unavailable: Serial proxy ports cannot be read here. Check that the USB and ESPHome integrations are set up.
error.unsupported_settings: The AUX-2 port does not accept these settings. Check the baud rate, data bits, parity and stop bits expected by the devices on the line.

data_description.proxy_device: Only AUX-2 devices adopted in Home Assistant show up here, with the serial ports they expose.

aux2.description: Choose the AUX-2 whose serial port this gateway connects through. Devices behind it are added to this connection afterwards.
aux2.title: Home Assistant Connect AUX-2

data_description.device: AUX-2 ports are RS-232: a Modbus bus on RS-485 needs an adapter between it and this port.
data_description.parity: None, even or odd, as the devices on the line expect.

aux2_port.description: Choose the port of the AUX-2 to connect through, and how it talks to the devices wired to it. The port is opened once to check the settings before anything is stored.
aux2_port.title: Serial port

data_description.device_id: Changing the device ID moves this device. Its entity ids, unique ids and device id are kept, so history and dashboards follow it.
data_description.expected_offline: A device that is switched off by itself, such as a solar inverter after dark, reports being unavailable as information rather than as a fault. It is still read less often while it is off, and its entities are still unavailable.
